items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Man, I made plenty of records with Richard M Jones.

ctx.x: Met him in New York or in California? No, New York. I see. Did you ever know Richard M Jones?

Yeah, I made records with him. Richard M Jones, crippled fellow. Yeah, played piano. Where did you make the records with him? And John had none of them records? Man, I made plenty of records with Richard M Jones. No, I don't have any of the ones you made with him. Mr. Bill didn't have none? He probably does, somewhere hidden. He must be got them records. Man, all his own stuff though, you know, he was writing out his stuff himself, you know. He could write out some nice stuff boy, Richard M Jones. Yeah, crippled…
You played jobs with him, spot jobs? Yeah, but you know, not gigs I mean, not going to run one steady job. You remember he was in the band with you with Richard M Jones,

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: But I made plenty of records with him.

ctx.x: Because I think we played the record for you one time. Yeah. And you remember that.

Manny, That's that fellow I played the record with him. Manny something. Manny, not Manny Thomas, Manny something. You all know him but he was kind of well known. Manny, Manny. But I made plenty of records with him. He'd just sit down and write a little old number, you know, and just go out on and play them and put on the record. Manny Jones. Oh Richard M. Jones. Richard M. Jones. That's his name. We used to call him Manny.
Well I made plenty of records.
